tasks.title: Foundation and contracts
tasks.goal: Bootstrap the repository, typed settings, architectural references, and fresh-session workflow so later implementation slices share the same contracts and operating assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: A uv-managed Python package exists under src/weather_agent with baseline tooling and placeholder tests.
Typed configuration loads required secrets and settings without logging sensitive values.
Architecture ADRs and domain vocabulary document the MVP boundaries and core contracts.
Agent workflow guidance is explicit about Beads, fresh sessions, testing, and deterministic rule evaluation.
tests: uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
tasks.rollout: Land this slice first and keep later work blocked until package layout, settings, and ADR vocabulary are stable.
tasks.observability: Baseline logging should avoid secrets and make configuration failures obvious during local startup.
tasks.notes: Maps directly to WA-001, WA-002, WA-003, and WA-035; assumes the repository can adopt a fresh src-layout without preserving legacy runtime code.

tasks.title: Deployment and persistence base
tasks.goal: Create the runnable local stack and database migration baseline needed by all stateful services.
acceptance_criteria: Docker Compose config defines the bot or API service, worker service, and Postgres TimescaleDB service with viable health checks.
Initial migrations create the relational and time-series tables needed by the epic with indexes and JSON payload support.
Local startup instructions cover first-run configuration and database bring-up.
tests: docker compose config
docker compose up postgres-timescaledb
migration smoke test against a disposable database
tasks.rollout: Treat migrations and Compose as a stable base; later slices should extend rather than rewrite these contracts.
tasks.observability: Startup and migration logs should clearly expose connection failures, invalid env vars, and schema drift.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-004 and WA-005 and should finish before any DB-backed domain or provider work is considered stable.

tasks.title: Core domain services
tasks.goal: Implement authorization, settings, locations, deterministic time resolution, and normalized weather contracts that the application and adapters can share.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization and global settings services are independent of Telegram library types.
Locations support aliases, coordinates, lifecycle flags, and duplicate-conflict protection.
DateResolver deterministically maps Polish time phrases into explicit Europe/Warsaw ranges with explanation text.
Forecast, observation, and warning contracts use normalized unit-qualified fields and preserve raw provider payloads.
tests: unit tests for authorization and global settings
unit tests for location CRUD and alias resolution
frozen-clock tests for DateResolver
model serialization tests for normalized weather contracts
tasks.rollout: Freeze these contracts before writing adapters or graph nodes so later implementation can treat them as durable boundaries.
tasks.observability: Domain-level validation errors should be typed and surfaced without stack traces leaking into user-facing flows.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-006 through WA-009 and assumes Polish-only language plus Europe/Warsaw timezone remain hard MVP constraints.

tasks.title: Weather ingestion and storage
tasks.goal: Add provider adapters, normalized persistence, and snapshot utilities so the system can fetch, store, and compare forecast and warning data deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: Open-Meteo DWD ICON forecasts normalize into shared contracts with typed timeout and retry behavior.
IMGW synop and official-warning adapters parse source payloads without fabricating missing values.
Forecasts, observations, warnings, and raw payloads persist with queryable normalized fields.
Snapshot comparison utilities provide typed delta outputs suitable for later rule evaluation.
tests: mocked HTTP tests for Open-Meteo and IMGW adapters
integration tests for weather-data repositories
unit tests for forecast snapshot comparison behavior
tasks.rollout: Keep provider interfaces independent from Telegram and LangGraph so failures stay isolated to adapter boundaries.
tasks.observability: Provider calls should emit structured success and failure metadata with enough detail to diagnose drift or throttling.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-010 through WA-014 and assumes Open-Meteo DWD ICON plus IMGW remain the only required MVP providers.

tasks.title: Rule runtime
tasks.goal: Implement deterministic CEL-backed rule creation, evaluation, cooldown handling, and persisted explanation evidence without depending on the LLM at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: CEL validation enforces a strict allowlist of functions, variables, and metrics.
Rules persist with short IDs, lifecycle metadata, and validated expressions only.
Evaluation worker runs deterministically against persisted weather snapshots and produces explainable events.
Cooldown, dedupe, snooze, and audit behavior prevent noisy or duplicated notifications.
tests: unit tests for CEL validation and evaluation
repository tests for rule CRUD and event persistence
worker tests for cooldown, dedupe, and explanation data
tasks.rollout: Do not expose user-facing rule flows until deterministic validation, persistence, and worker execution all pass.
tasks.observability: Every evaluation run and emitted notification candidate should be traceable through durable IDs and structured audit records.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-015 through WA-019 and preserves the non-negotiable constraint that LLM output may propose rules but never execute them.

tasks.title: Telegram channel
tasks.goal: Build the Telegram ingress and egress layer, including authorization, thread context isolation, deterministic commands, and delivery plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized Telegram messages enter the application layer while unauthorized traffic is denied or ignored safely.
Thread context keys isolate state by chat and topic and route notifications back to the origin thread by default.
Deterministic commands for locations and rules work without requiring the LLM.
Notification sending preserves short IDs and avoids leaking secrets or internal errors.
tests: unit tests for unauthorized message handling
tests covering topic and non-topic context mapping
command-handler tests for location and rule operations
sender tests for formatted notification delivery
tasks.rollout: Enable Telegram flows only after the rule runtime and core domain services can back them with deterministic behavior.
tasks.observability: Inbound updates, authorization denials, command routing, and outbound sends should all leave structured traces and audit markers.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-020 through WA-023 and assumes Telegram private supergroup plus Topics remains the recommended operating environment.

tasks.title: LangGraph orchestration and observability
tasks.goal: Wire provider-agnostic model selection, typed conversational state, graph flows, thread-scoped memory, tracing, logging, health surfaces, retention jobs, and production-like stack finishing work.
acceptance_criteria: Model configuration is provider-agnostic and defaults to gpt-5-mini without hard-coding a single vendor throughout the app.
LangGraph state and graph skeleton support weather and rule-confirmation paths with typed state objects.
Weather Q&A, rule proposal, pending confirmations, tracing, logging, and status flows work together without making correctness depend on LangSmith availability.
Retention jobs, health surfaces, and production-like Compose wiring support operating the stack in a homelab environment.
tests: graph-path tests for weather and rule-confirmation routes
tests for pending confirmation persistence and retrieval
LangSmith wiring tests or smoke checks with tracing toggled on
status and cleanup job tests
docker compose config for the production-like stack
tasks.rollout: Land graph and observability slices behind stable provider, domain, and Telegram seams so orchestration bugs do not force contract rewrites.
tasks.observability: Graph path, tool calls, evaluation IDs, cleanup activity, and status surfaces should make it possible to debug failures without replaying user conversations manually.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-024 through WA-034 except eval and release tasks; LangSmith is required for learning visibility but not for deterministic runtime correctness.

tasks.title: Verification and release
tasks.goal: Prove the MVP end to end with eval assets, mocked integration coverage, real-provider smoke checks, and deployment-ready documentation.
acceptance_criteria: A mocked end-to-end test covers location creation, weather Q&A, rule proposal and confirmation, evaluation, notification delivery, and later explanation.
Eval assets exercise intent classification and CEL generation quality for the main Polish-language flows.
Real-provider smoke checks confirm Open-Meteo and IMGW integrations against live services within safe limits.
Final documentation enables a new developer to deploy, configure, operate, back up, and verify the MVP from scratch.
tests: mocked end-to-end MVP test
LangSmith or pytest eval run
real-provider smoke test
documentation walkthrough against docker compose up
tasks.rollout: Treat this as the release gate; if mocked E2E or real-provider smoke checks fail, roll back to the latest passing phase and repair the underlying slice before shipping.
tasks.observability: Verification artifacts should link failures back to graph traces, provider logs, and persisted evaluation or notification records.
tasks.notes: Maps to WA-030, WA-036, WA-037, and WA-038 and assumes the Beads child backlog remains the execution source of truth below this release gate.
